completeness.why: getDateWithSkippedWeekend now takes the rule object and decides both whether it applies (skipWeekend) and the mode; getUpcomingDates passes its config, both schedule-template sites pass dateConditions.value to the day-string wrapper getDayWithSkippedWeekend, and getNextDate passes its parsed schedule data, keeping only its own noSkipWeekend guard, an option no other site has.

interface.why: A single rule parameter (skipWeekend + weekendSolveMode) covers the real variation and a thin day-string variant serves the template, with no speculative options, but instead of letting each caller map its own mode field it renames the parsed schedule's weekendSolve to weekendSolveMode in rule-utils, changing internal data shape to fit the helper.

disguised_duplication.where: The skipWeekend/mode ternaries are removed from all callers; getDayWithSkippedWeekend only adds the string conversion around the shared function (its early skipWeekend return is a short-circuit, not a separate rule).
